subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Should third-party plugin installation be allowed to request core configuration changes, and which single consented setup API should own that authority?
rationale: Current installation deliberately limits configuration mutations to plugin-owned enablement and install state, while existing broader patches occur in interactive provider setup; expanding this authority requires explicit product and security intent.

options.title: Unified typed setup intents
options.body: Add one allowlisted setup-intent contract for tool, service, provider, and hook plugins with visible diffs, explicit consent, validation, provenance, and recovery guidance.

options.title: Interactive setup hook only
options.body: Require plugins to expose a post-install setup step that returns guarded changes instead of declaring mutations in the manifest.

options.title: Keep manual configuration
options.body: Do not grant plugins authority over core configuration and retain plugin-specific setup documentation or CLI commands.

recommendation.title: Unified typed setup intents
recommendation.body: Add one allowlisted setup-intent contract for tool, service, provider, and hook plugins with visible diffs, explicit consent, validation, provenance, and recovery guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The central install-persistence and guarded configuration-mutation architecture traces most directly to this contributor's commits.
